intent.title: Timeline panel: create animations for an element
steps: Select a Heading and open the Timeline panel.
Create a second animation and rename and delete it.
expected: View > Timeline opens the Timeline panel as a tab in the bottom workbench.
The Timeline panel lists the animations of the selected element with a time ruler.
New animations are stored in the document JSON with a unique keyframes name, a 1 s duration and keyframes at 0% and 100%.
Rename and delete are undo steps; a deleted animation leaves no animation properties on the element.

intent.title: Add, edit, move and delete keyframes on the timeline
steps: Select the 'fade-in' animation, move the playhead to 50% and click 'Add keyframe' [timeline.addKeyframe].
With the playhead on the 0% keyframe set opacity 0 and Move Y 20px in the inspector; on 100% set opacity 1 and Move Y 0.
Drag the 50% keyframe to 30%; set its easing to ease-out; delete it.
expected: Keyframes show as diamonds on the track at their percentage.
While the playhead sits on a keyframe the inspector edits that keyframe's values (a badge says so) and not the base styles.
Keyframe offsets, values and per-keyframe easing are stored in the document JSON; moving and deleting are undo steps.

intent.title: Animation duration, delay, repeat, direction and fill
steps: Set duration 800 ms, delay 200 ms, iteration count infinite, direction alternate, fill mode both, timing function ease-in-out and play state paused, then running.
expected: Each setting is stored with the animation in the document JSON.
The animation has no trigger setting of its own.

intent.title: Preview animations by playing and scrubbing the timeline
steps: Click Play on the 'fade-in' animation, then Pause, then Stop.
expected: Play animates the element on the canvas using the stored keyframes; Pause freezes it; Stop returns it to its base styles.
Scrubbing shows the interpolated state at the playhead: at 50% of a linear 0-to-1 opacity animation the computed opacity is 0.5.
Previewing never changes the document JSON.

intent.title: Export animations as @keyframes
steps: Build an element with the 'fade-in' animation and settings, and export.
expected: styles.css contains @keyframes fade-in with every keyframe and its values, and the animation properties on the element's base rule, so the animation plays when the page loads.
A @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block turns the animations off; it is written only when the page has animations, so pages without animations export exactly as before.
In the exported page the element's computed animation-name is fade-in and two exports are byte-identical.

intent.title: Events and actions per element
steps: Select a Button, open the Interactions section and add: on click, toggle the class 'is-open' on a Container.

Add: on hover, show a hidden element; on scroll into view, play the 'fade-in' animation; on page load, scroll to an element; on submit of a Form, hide the form and show a message; on click, open a link in a new tab.
expected: Triggers are click, hover (enter and leave), scroll into view, page load and form submit; actions are show, hide, toggle class, play animation, scroll to and open link.
Targets are picked from the page or Layers, never typed ids; combinations that cannot apply (form submit on a non-form) are not offered.
Interactions are stored per element in the document JSON; each add, edit and remove is one undo step.
The editing canvas never runs them.

intent.title: Export interactions as standard JavaScript
steps: Build the interactions of events-actions, preview the page and trigger each event, then export.
expected: The ZIP contains the plain JavaScript file js/interactions.js (no framework, no inline handlers), linked with <script defer> from every page that uses interactions.
Targets are addressed by their BEM class or user id, never by editor ids or data attributes.
An animation played by an event gets a class rule in styles.css, next to its @keyframes, that the script adds when the event fires.
Preview runs every interaction exactly like the exported page; an animation used by a play-animation action no longer plays on page load and plays when its event fires.
In the exported page opened in Chrome every trigger performs its action, checked by class, computed style or scroll position.
Pages without interactions export exactly as before, with no script.
